details: The Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 3.50%-3.75% but adopted a more hawkish outlook. Nine of eighteen Fed officials now project at least one rate hike in 2026, and the Fed abandoned forward guidance, emphasizing price stability. This hawkish shift triggered a significant sell-off in risk assets, including cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin dropped below $64,000, and over $361 million in crypto long positions were liquidated across exchanges within 24 hours.
title: Hawkish Fed Stance Fuels Crypto Sell-off and Liquidations

details: The US Dollar Index (DXY) has climbed above 101, reaching its highest level since May 2025. This resurgence of dollar strength typically has an inverse correlation with Bitcoin prices, as a stronger dollar makes dollar-denominated assets relatively more attractive and tightens global financial conditions, weighing on risk-sensitive assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: US Dollar Index Rises, Pressuring Bitcoin and Risk Assets

details: Bitcoin's volatility index (BVIV), often referred to as a "fear gauge," surged 20% in the last 24 hours to 46.45%. This marks the largest single-day jump since a crypto crash in February, reflecting increased investor nervousness and anxiety as the cryptocurrency sell-off intensifies and Bitcoin trades near $66,000.
title: Bitcoin's 'Fear Gauge' Spikes Amid Deepening Sell-off

details: Concerns over strained US-Iran negotiations and ongoing Israeli missile strikes in Lebanon are contributing to bearish pressure on the broader cryptocurrency market. Bitcoin slipped below $63,000, with altcoins like Bitcoin Cash and Hyperliquid also experiencing significant losses in the last 24 hours.
title: Geopolitical Tensions Add Pressure to Crypto Market
